A baked vanilla custard under a thin layer of caramelised sugar. Make the custards a day ahead and caramelise the sugar just before serving.

== Ingredients ==
''Serves 4''
* 500 ml double (heavy) cream
* 1 vanilla pod, or 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
* 5 egg yolks
* 60 g caster sugar, plus about 4 teaspoons for the tops
* A pinch of salt

== Method ==
# Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Put four ramekins in a deep roasting tin and boil a kettle.
# Split the vanilla pod, scrape out the seeds and warm them with the pod and the cream until steaming. Do not let it boil. Take it off the heat, leave it for 10 minutes, then remove the pod.
# Whisk the yolks, 60 g sugar and salt until just combined. Slowly pour in the warm cream, whisking all the time.
# Strain the custard through a fine sieve into a jug and skim off any foam.
# Divide between the ramekins. Pour hot water into the tin to come halfway up their sides.
# Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until set at the edges with a gentle wobble in the centre.
# Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
# To serve, sprinkle about 1 teaspoon of sugar over each custard and caramelise it with a kitchen torch, or under a very hot grill.

== Tips ==
* Whisk the yolks gently. Air bubbles give a pitted surface.
* Use the leftover whites for meringues.
